free_tier.stated: Paid-only, five plans on the front page: 40G KVM with 40 GB RAID-10 SSD, 2 GiB RAM, 3x Intel Xeon, 2 TB/mo, 1 Gigabit at USD 52.99 per half-year; 80G with 80 GB RAID-10 SSD, 4 GiB RAM, 4x Intel Xeon, 3 TB/mo at USD 19.99 a month; 160G with 160 GB RAID-10 SSD, 8 GiB RAM, 5x Intel Xeon, 4 TB/mo at USD 39.99 a month; 320G with 320 GB RAID-10 SSD, 16 GiB RAM, 6x Intel Xeon, 5 TB/mo at USD 79.99 a month; and 480G with 480 GB RAID-10 SSD, 24 GiB RAM, 7x Intel Xeon, 6 TB/mo at USD 119.99 a month. All plans are self-managed KVM on KiwiVM, which allows start/stop, OS reload, Emergency console, rDNS (PTR) record management, datacenter migration, snapshots, usage statistics and API.

chaining: The datacenter-migration feature is worth more than the price: a box that can be moved between locations without reinstalling is the cheapest way to test which region a workload actually needs.

limits.value: One terabyte a month is the term that binds, and the plan is annual, so an overrun is corrected only at renewal. The plan is unmanaged: the vendor states self-managed KVM, so a broken image is the buyer's problem and there is no managed support tier at this price.
